setup: Laptop, Ollama. The demo scenario: two ChatGPT exports, a meeting transcript and a Claude Code session, scored against a 10-item gold list.

extraction.what: Precision is the share of proposed entries the reviewer settled. Before: phase 1, no feedback. After: phase 2, on unseen conversations, with the rules learned from phase 1 rejections.

rows.run: no extraction mistakes, so nothing to learn

checks.cases: Three real contradictions and three non-contradictions, two of them "add a cache in front of the database" traps.

rows.note: Both cache traps flagged as contradictions
The critic drops both false alarms

checks.critic: The critic runs only when the first pass claims a conflict. It asks whether the new work stops using, migrates away from or goes against what was chosen, and reasons before it answers.

dogfood.what: The Claude Code session in which Sthira was built
dogfood.model: qwen3.8-27b, with gpt-oss-120b as fallback, on a free hosted tier
right: The project will be named Sthira
The pitch should not rely on the 'Hacktoberfest PR' angle because PRs no longer earn rewards in the 2026 program
The tool will run on a local open-weight model to ensure user data privacy
wrong: Several entries are conversation chatter attributed to "the user", such as "The user prefers the assistant to continue work autonomously".
An earlier run on qwen3:4b recorded "use Stet as the project name", a name we later dropped. The Sthira decision supersedes it and the history stays.
dogfood.bug: The run also found a real bug: a first pass read only 17 of 143 messages and skipped the rest silently. Fixed in PR #17.

limits: One small scenario, built by the same team that built the system: smoke-test numbers, not a benchmark.
The reviewer is simulated (a keyword match against gold) and judges borderline items strictly.
Runs are not seeded, so expect variation between runs, especially on 4B models.
